name: Gertrude Ederle
highlight: First woman across the Channel · Friday 6 August 1926
biography: Gertrude Caroline “Trudy” Ederle was born in New York City on 23 October 1905. A member of the Women’s Swimming Association, she developed into a leading freestyle swimmer before turning to long-distance challenges. At the 1924 Paris Olympics she won gold in the 4 × 100 metres freestyle relay and bronze in both the 100 and 400 metres freestyle. Her bronze in the 400 metres came in 6 minutes 4.8 seconds, behind her American teammates Martha Norelius and Helen Wainwright. She had already set long-course world records in the 400 metres in 1922 and the 200 metres in 1923.

On Friday 6 August 1926 Ederle became the first woman to swim the English Channel. She swam front crawl from Cap Gris-Nez to Kingsdown and beat the previous fastest crossing by a man. Her registered time is 14 hours 39 minutes.

The detailed Dover crossing log gives 07:05 at Cap Gris-Nez and 21:44 at Kingsdown. A second historical register gives 06:09 and 20:48. Both clock pairs span 14 hours 39 minutes, and neither entry names its time standard. Dover Museum gives 14 hours 34 minutes in Between Wars and 14 hours 33 minutes in Records & Firsts. The log lists Joe Costa with Thomas Burgess aboard Alsace, accompanied by the press tug La Morinie. It records retrospective recognition on 16 August 1928.

On 27 August 1926, she returned to New York aboard the Berengaria and was welcomed with a ticker-tape parade. City records preserve the reception committee’s minutes, letters and photographs, including her reception aboard the municipal steamer Macom. The welcome carried her sporting achievement into the city’s civic history.
Later in life, she taught swimming to deaf children, extending her contribution to swimming beyond her competitive achievements.

Dover Museum accounts
lines.text: Between Wars gives 14h34. Records & Firsts gives 14h33. Both identify Ederle as the first woman to cross.

lines.label: Contemporary reports
lines.text: The Associated Press account preserved in the Capital Journal gives 07:09–21:40 and 14h31. TIME also reported 14h31. The Manchester Guardian’s report of 7 August instead printed 14h45.

lines.label: French archival account
lines.text: The Pas-de-Calais departmental archive gives 14h32. Its narrative gives 07:05 and 21:33, which span 14h28 on one clock. The elapsed figure and the clock pair are retained separately.

CSA record 2236 identifies Ederle, United States, solo France to England and 14h39. CS&PF historical entry 442807 names the CSA as ratifier and gives the same elapsed time. The Dover swim entry records independent observation followed by CSA recognition on 16 August 1928. These sources establish the crossing and its registered duration. Accounts disagree on the clocks.

otherEvents.title: Paris Olympics — women’s 4 × 100 m freestyle relay

lines.text: USA won gold in a team world-record time of 4:58.8; Ederle swam the second leg.
